title: House Tied to Five Overdose Deaths Since 2023 Torn Down in Laredo
excerpt: A house at the corner of Sanders Avenue and Olive Street that Laredo police linked to years of drug activity and at least five overdose deaths since 2023 was torn down Wednesday, Nov. 25, as neighbors watched.
content:
A house at the corner of Sanders Avenue and Olive Street that Laredo police linked to years of drug activity and at least five overdose deaths was torn down on Wednesday, Nov. 25, as neighbors watched an excavator break through its walls.

At least five people have died of overdoses connected to the property since 2023, Laredo Police Department investigator and spokesperson Joe Baeza told the Laredo Morning Times. Three were found dead at the home, including one by the porch, and two others died after being taken from the house to a hospital, he said.

Police said fentanyl was among the drugs dealt or kept at the home, and that reports of drug activity and overdoses at the address go back to 2003. Plans to demolish the house had been in the works for more than a year, and authorities first had to complete a lengthy process to declare the site dangerous before machinery could move in.

Homeland Security Investigations, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the U.S. Border Patrol and the Webb County Constable's Office Precinct 1 joined Laredo police at the site as a contractor's excavator tore the structure down.

Neighbors called the demolition an answered prayer, according to KGNS, saying the home had been a danger to the neighborhood for years. Inside, officers documented rooms filled with trash and items associated with drug use, including a burnt soda can and a spoon with residue.

Police also investigated a 2025 death near East Olive Street and Sanders Avenue involving a man identified only as John Doe. That death was ruled an overdose, with no foul play suspected.

The Laredo Police Department posted video of the demolition on Nov. 25, calling it a “Drug House Demo Day” and saying the department is committed to safer neighborhoods.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 25, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 25, 2026; Laredo Police Department, Nov. 25, 2026; Local National: Police Tear Down Home Tied to Five Overdose Deaths Since 2023.
